newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - TIMELINES-Today in History - Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - TIMELINES-Today in History - Sept 16.

text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
Australian politician RICHARD DRIVER was born in 1829. A great cricket fan, the street running along the front of the Sydney Cricket Ground was called Driver Avenue.
Australian mountaineer FREDA DU FAUR, who was the first woman to climb New Zealand's Mount Cook, was born in 1882. She climbed in skirts and with a chaperone. No text received
Hungarian-born film producer Sir ALEXANDER KORDA, who brought us "The Third Man", "The Scarlet Pimpernel" and "Four Feathers", was born in 1893.
American actress LAUREN BACALL, who made her debut in "To Have and Have Not", was born in 1924. She starred opposite her future husband HUMPHREY BOGART.
American blues guitarist B.B. KING was born in 1925. He was an inspiration to a whole generation of rock musicians including ERIC CLAPTON.
UK drummer KENNY JONES, who played with the 'Small Faces', 'Faces', 'The Who' and ROD STEWART, was born in 1948.
US singer,guitarist, keyboard player and songwriter with the 'Bellamy Brothers', DAVID BELLAMY, was born in 1950.
**EVENTS**
1908 : In the United States, General Motors was formed by
the merger of Buick and Oldsmobile.
1920 : A bomb blast on New York's Wall Street killed 30
people and injured another 300. Russian ALEXANDER BRAILOVSKY was arrested two days later for the bombing.
1932 : Severe earthquakes rocked Poverty Bay and Hawkes
Bay districts in New Zealand.
1944 : A New Zealand sapper (soldier in the engineering
corp) missing in Greece for three years, reported for duty after being in hiding for the entire time.
1947 : The Victorian health department introduced free
X-Rays for TB.
1956 : Australia's first regular television service was
launched by TCN 9 in Sydney. BRUCE GYNGELL, was the first face on the screen. Transmissions followed by HSV Channel 7, GTV Channel and ABC Channel 2.
1961 : St.George won a record sixth Rugby League
premiership in a row. They defeated Souths 22-0 in the Grand Final at the Sydney Cricket Ground.
1963 : Malaysia became independent and a mob of more than
100,000 burnt down the British Embassy in celebration.
1974 : US President FORD pardoned his predecessor RICHARD
NIXON for his part in the Watergate affair. NIXON resigned after being suspected of criminal involvement in the break-in at the Democratic headquarters.
1977 : Lead singer of 'T-Rex', MARC BOLAN, died in a car
crash.
1987 : More than 70 countries agreed on measures to
reduce the threat to the earth's ozone layer. The parties agreed to freeze chlorofluorocarbon use at the 1987 levels and reduce use by half by 1999.
1988 : Thousands of Americans rushed to apply for a new
credit card featuring the King of Rock. The ELVIS PRESLEY credit card allowed customers credit of up to $3500.
1991 : A man attacked MICHELANGELO's Statue of DAVID,

breaking off the second toe on the left foot. The 4 metre sculpture is one of the great masterpieces of Renaissance art. The attacker told Florence police he was merely following instructions from "Nani" a Venetian model in the 16th century.
1994 : The Exxon Corporation to pay five-billion dollars
in punitive damages, over the 1989 oil spill off the Alaskan coast.
